references.text: The psalm prophesies that God will not let his Holy One see decay – a messianic text about the resurrection which the disciples came to believe after Jesus' resurrection ([ref:Ps 16:10|Psalm 16:10]).
Jesus' words about tearing down the temple and raising it up in three days – this is the statement the disciples remembered after the resurrection ([ref:John 2:19|John 2:19]).

Here too, it is told that the disciples only after Jesus' glorification remembered what had been written about him and what they had done, parallel to how they remembered his words after the resurrection ([ref:John 12:16|John 12:16]).

Jesus promises that the Holy Spirit will remind the disciples of all he has said – this explains how they were able to remember and understand his words after the resurrection ([ref:John 14:26|John 14:26]).

At the empty tomb, it is noted that the disciples still had not understood the Scripture that Jesus must rise from the dead – this connects directly to the belief in Scripture mentioned after the temple cleansing ([ref:John 20:9|John 20:9]).

After the resurrection, the angels remind the women of what Jesus had said while he was still in Galilee, and they remembered his words – a clear parallel to how the disciples remembered Jesus' words after the resurrection ([ref:Luke 24:6-8|Luke 24:6-8]).

Peter quotes Psalm 16 in his Pentecost sermon and applies it to Jesus' resurrection – an example of how the disciples, after the resurrection, believed both Scripture and Jesus' words ([ref:Acts 2:31-32|Acts 2:31-32]).

Paul confesses that Christ was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures – this shows the apostolic belief in Scripture regarding the resurrection, just as the disciples came to believe after Jesus' resurrection ([ref:1 Cor 15:4|1 Corinthians 15:4]).
